title: Isaiah Chapter 29 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 29 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 29 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 29.

questions.question: In Isaiah 29, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Woe to Ariel, the city where David dwelt
The multitude of thy strangers shall be like small dust
Thou shalt be visited of the LORD of hosts with thunder and earthquake
The multitude of all the nations that fight against Ariel shall be as a dream
questions.correctAnswer: Woe to Ariel, the city where David dwelt
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:1 begins with 'Woe to Ariel, to Ariel, the city where David dwelt!' which is the earliest event mentioned in the chapter.

questions.question: What city is referred to as Ariel in Isaiah 29:1?
questions.correctAnswer: The city where David dwelt
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:1 states 'Ariel, the city where David dwelt'.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 29:2, what shall be unto the LORD as Ariel?
options: The speech out of the dust
questions.correctAnswer: The heaviness and sorrow
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:2 says 'there shall be heaviness and sorrow: and it shall be unto me as Ariel.'

questions.question: What does God say He will do against Ariel in Isaiah 29:3?
options: Camp against thee round about and lay siege
questions.correctAnswer: Camp against thee round about and lay siege
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:3 states 'And I will camp against thee round about, and will lay siege against thee with a mount, and I will raise forts against thee.'

questions.question: In Isaiah 29:4, how is the speech of Ariel described after being brought down?
options: Low out of the dust, whispering as one that hath a familiar spirit
Loud and proud from the mountains
questions.correctAnswer: Low out of the dust, whispering as one that hath a familiar spirit
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:4 says 'thy speech shall be low out of the dust, and thy voice shall be, as of one that hath a familiar spirit, out of the ground, and thy speech shall whisper out of the dust.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 29:5, the multitude of thy strangers shall be like what?
questions.correctAnswer: Small dust
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:5 states 'Moreover the multitude of thy strangers shall be like small dust.'

questions.question: Isaiah 29:6 describes the LORD of hosts visiting with all EXCEPT which of the following?
questions.correctAnswer: Peaceful rain
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:6 mentions thunder, earthquake, great noise, storm, tempest, and flame of devouring fire, but not peaceful rain.

questions.question: The multitude of all nations fighting against Ariel shall be like what, according to Isaiah 29:7?
options: A dream of a night vision
questions.correctAnswer: A dream of a night vision
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:7 says 'shall be as a dream of a night vision.'

questions.question: How does Isaiah 29:8 describe the dreams of a hungry and thirsty man?
options: He eateth and drinketh but awaketh faint and empty
He feasts and drinks fully awake
He ignores his hunger and thirst
He finds no satisfaction even in dreams
questions.correctAnswer: He eateth and drinketh but awaketh faint and empty
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:8 says the hungry man dreameth he eateth but awaketh and his soul is empty; the thirsty man dreameth he drinketh but awaketh faint and hungry.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 29:1, what are they commanded to do year to year?
options: Add ye year to year; let them kill sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: Add ye year to year; let them kill sacrifices
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:1 says 'add ye year to year; let them kill sacrifices.'

questions.question: Isaiah 29:3 mentions that God will raise what against Ariel?
questions.correctAnswer: Forts
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:3 states 'I will raise forts against thee.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 29:6 says the LORD of hosts will visit Ariel with storm and tempest.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:6 states 'Thou shalt be visited of the LORD of hosts with thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with storm and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 29:7 says that all nations fighting against Ariel will be as a dream of a night vision.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:7 states 'the multitude of all the nations that fight against Ariel... shall be as a dream of a night vision.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 29 says that Ariel will be visited by peaceful rain from the LORD of hosts.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:6 describes the LORD's visitation with thunder, earthquake, great noise, storm, tempest, and devouring fire, but does not mention peaceful rain.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 29:8 says that the multitude of nations fighting against mount Zion will be victorious and strong.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:8 compares the nations fighting against mount Zion to a hungry man dreaming he eats but awakens empty, indicating their efforts will be in vain.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 29 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 29 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What condition do the people of Ariel find themselves in according to Isaiah 29:9?
options: They are drunken, but not with wine
questions.correctAnswer: They are drunken, but not with wine
questions.explanation: This is correct as Isaiah 29:9 states, 'they are drunken, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink.'

questions.question: What does Isaiah 29:10 promise will happen if someone draws near to God with their heart?
options: They will be given deep sleep
questions.correctAnswer: They will be given deep sleep
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:10 indicates that the LORD has poured out the spirit of deep sleep upon the people, implying a lack of true connection with Him.

questions.question: What happened to the vision according to Isaiah 29:11?
options: It became as the words of a book that is sealed
questions.correctAnswer: It became as the words of a book that is sealed
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:11 describes the vision as sealed, making it inaccessible to those who seek to understand it.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 29:12 indicate about a man who is not learned when given the book?
options: He will read it with joy
He will say, 'I am not learned'
He will refuse to read it
questions.correctAnswer: He will say, 'I am not learned'
questions.explanation: According to Isaiah 29:12, the unlearned man responds by saying he cannot read because he is not learned.

questions.question: In Isaiah 29:13, what does the Lord say about the people's worship?
options: They honor Him with their lips, but their hearts are far from Him
They are faithful in their prayers
questions.correctAnswer: They honor Him with their lips, but their hearts are far from Him
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:13 highlights the disconnect between external worship and the true state of their hearts.

questions.question: What does the Lord promise to do in Isaiah 29:14?
options: Perform a marvelous work and a wonder
questions.correctAnswer: Perform a marvelous work and a wonder
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:14 states that the Lord will proceed to do a marvelous work among the people, indicating a significant intervention.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 29:15, what is the consequence for those who seek to hide their counsel from the Lord?
options: They will succeed in their plans
questions.correctAnswer: They will be found out
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:15 warns that those who hide their counsel from the Lord will not escape His notice.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 29:16 say about the relationship between the creator and the created?
options: The created can question the creator
The creator is always understood by the created
The created cannot claim independence from the creator
The creator is irrelevant to the created
questions.correctAnswer: The created cannot claim independence from the creator
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:16 illustrates that the created cannot say to the creator, 'He made me not,' emphasizing the inherent relationship.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 29:4 describe the speech of the people?
options: It shall be low out of the dust
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be low out of the dust
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:4 portrays the people's speech as low and humble, reflecting their fallen state.

questions.question: What imagery does Isaiah 29:8 use to describe the nations that fight against Ariel?
options: They are as strong as lions
They are like a dream of a night vision
They are as numerous as the stars
questions.correctAnswer: They are like a dream of a night vision
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:8 uses the imagery of a dream to emphasize the fleeting and insubstantial nature of the nations' efforts against Ariel.

questions.question: In practical terms, what does Isaiah 29:13 suggest about the nature of true worship?
options: It should come from the heart
questions.correctAnswer: It should come from the heart
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:13 indicates that honoring God must not just be lip service but should involve a genuine heart connection.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 29:10 imply about spiritual blindness?
options: It is a punishment from God
It is a natural state of being
questions.correctAnswer: It is a punishment from God
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:10 implies that the spirit of deep sleep and closed eyes is a result of the Lord's action, indicating a form of judgment.

questions.question: Is it true that according to Isaiah 29:14, the wisdom of the wise men will perish?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:14 states that the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, indicating that human wisdom is limited.

questions.question: Is it false that Isaiah 29:6 speaks of a peaceful visit from the Lord?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:6 describes a tumultuous visit from the Lord with thunder and earthquake, not a peaceful one.

questions.question: Is it false that according to Isaiah 29:5, the multitude of nations will succeed against Ariel?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:5 states that the multitude of nations shall be like small dust, indicating their futility against Ariel.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 29 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 29.

questions.question: What will Lebanon be turned into according to Isaiah 29:17?
questions.correctAnswer: A fruitful field
questions.explanation: According to Isaiah 29:17, Lebanon shall be turned into a fruitful field, indicating a transformation from barrenness to productivity.

questions.question: Who shall hear the words of the book in that day as stated in Isaiah 29:18?
questions.correctAnswer: The deaf
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:18 states that in that day the deaf shall hear the words of the book, symbolizing a restoration of understanding and revelation.

questions.question: What will the poor among men do according to Isaiah 29:19?
options: Rejoice in the Holy One of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Rejoice in the Holy One of Israel
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 29:19, it is mentioned that the poor among men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel, highlighting a theme of hope and joy for the humble.

questions.question: What happens to the terrible one according to Isaiah 29:20?
questions.correctAnswer: He is brought to nought
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:20 reveals that the terrible one is brought to nought, emphasizing divine justice against oppressors.

questions.question: What shall happen to those who make a man an offender for a word as per Isaiah 29:21?
questions.correctAnswer: They will be cut off
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:21 indicates that those who lay snares for the just will be cut off, emphasizing the consequences of injustice.

questions.question: What is the significance of Jacob not being ashamed in Isaiah 29:22?
options: It signifies the end of suffering
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God's redemption
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:22 reassures that Jacob shall not be ashamed, highlighting God’s redemptive promise to His people.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Ariel' in Isaiah 29:1 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Altar hearth
questions.explanation: 'Ariel' in Hebrew means 'altar hearth', signifying the sacredness of the city and its connection to worship.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in Isaiah 29:18 when contrasting the deaf and the blind?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:18 employs parallelism by contrasting the deaf and the blind, enhancing the poetic structure and highlighting themes of restoration.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of the deaf hearing as stated in Isaiah 29:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 11:5
questions.explanation: Matthew 11:5 echoes the theme of the deaf hearing, fulfilling the prophetic promise found in Isaiah 29:18 regarding the miracles of Jesus.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of joy for the meek as stated in Isaiah 29:19?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 5:5
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:5 connects to Isaiah 29:19 by stating that the meek shall inherit the earth, reflecting the promise of joy for the humble.

questions.question: What comes directly before the statement in Isaiah 29:20?
options: The terrible one is brought to nought
questions.correctAnswer: The meek shall rejoice
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:20 follows the statement about the meek increasing their joy, indicating a continuation of the themes of justice and hope.

questions.question: In Isaiah 29:24, what will those who erred in spirit come to?
questions.correctAnswer: Understanding
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:24 states that those who erred in spirit shall come to understanding, emphasizing a theme of enlightenment and correction.

questions.question: In Isaiah 29:11, what is said about the vision of all?
questions.correctAnswer: It is sealed
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:11 indicates that the vision of all has become as sealed words, illustrating the people's inability to comprehend God's message.

questions.question: True or False: The eyes of the blind shall see out of darkness as stated in Isaiah 29:18.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:18 affirms that the eyes of the blind shall see out of darkness, symbolizing restoration and revelation.

questions.question: True or False: Jacob's face shall wax pale according to Isaiah 29:22.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:22 states that Jacob shall not now be ashamed, indicating that his face shall not wax pale, which emphasizes the assurance of God’s protection.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 29 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 29 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 29:13 teach about human sin?
options: Hypocrisy in worship where heart is far from God
Imputation of Adam's sin to all
questions.correctAnswer: Hypocrisy in worship where heart is far from God
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:13 states that the people honor God with their lips but have removed their heart far from Him, highlighting the doctrine of hypocritical worship.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine judgment is taught in Isaiah 29:6?
options: God’s judgment involves natural elements as instruments
God’s judgment is purely spiritual and invisible
Judgment is delayed until the final resurrection
God’s judgment is arbitrary and capricious
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment involves natural elements as instruments
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:6 describes the LORD visiting Ariel with thunder, earthquake, storm, and fire, indicating that God uses natural phenomena as means of judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine about prophetic revelation does Isaiah 29:11 teach?
options: God’s word can be sealed and hidden from the unfaithful
All prophecy is immediately clear to everyone
Prophecy is fallible and often incorrect
questions.correctAnswer: God’s word can be sealed and hidden from the unfaithful
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:11 speaks of the vision being like a sealed book that the learned cannot read, showing that God's revelation can be obscured from those not granted understanding.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 29:22 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:22 refers to the LORD who redeemed Abraham and promises Jacob will not be ashamed, highlighting God's covenant faithfulness to His people.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 29:10 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty in hardening hearts
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:10 shows the LORD pouring out a spirit of deep sleep and closing eyes, indicating His sovereign control over human understanding.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 29:18 connect to New Testament themes of spiritual enlightenment?
options: It prefigures the opening of spiritual eyes and ears through Christ
It contradicts the New Testament by focusing on physical healing only
It denies any future restoration of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the opening of spiritual eyes and ears through Christ
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:18 speaks of the deaf hearing and the blind seeing, prefiguring spiritual enlightenment fulfilled in Christ as described in the New Testament (e.g., John 9).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does Isaiah 29:1-2 prepare for?
options: The judgment and eventual restoration of Jerusalem
The exile of the northern kingdom only
The establishment of a new temple
questions.correctAnswer: The judgment and eventual restoration of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:1-2 pronounces woe against Ariel (Jerusalem) and foretells distress, fitting the theme of Jerusalem’s judgment and future restoration.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 29:13 and 29:14 teach about human wisdom and divine intervention?
options: Human wisdom is insufficient and God will overturn it with His marvelous work
Human wisdom is superior to divine revelation
God ignores human pride and lets it stand
questions.correctAnswer: Human wisdom is insufficient and God will overturn it with His marvelous work
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:13-14 together show that human wisdom is vain and God will do a marvelous work to confound the wise, emphasizing divine sovereignty over human understanding.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 29:15 and 29:16 teach about human sin and divine sovereignty?
options: Human attempts to hide sin are futile before God the Sovereign Creator
Human sin can be hidden from God indefinitely
God is ignorant of human rebellion
Creation claims independence from the Creator
questions.correctAnswer: Human attempts to hide sin are futile before God the Sovereign Creator
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:15-16 describe those trying to hide their counsel from God and turning things upside down, but God as potter sovereignly judges them.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 29:23 and 29:24 teach about sanctification and repentance?
options: God’s work in His people leads to sanctification and understanding
Those who err are beyond hope
questions.correctAnswer: God’s work in His people leads to sanctification and understanding
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:23-24 teach that God’s handiwork sanctifies His name and that those who erred will come to understanding, showing sanctification and repentance.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Isaiah 29:11-12 teaches that God’s word is unknowable and thus irrelevant. What does the passage actually teach?
options: God’s word is sealed to those who are not granted understanding, emphasizing human responsibility and divine sovereignty
God’s word is entirely secret and no one can understand it
Prophecy is meaningless and should be ignored
Only the educated elite can access God’s word
questions.correctAnswer: God’s word is sealed to those who are not granted understanding, emphasizing human responsibility and divine sovereignty
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:11-12 explains that the vision is like a sealed book that those who are not learned cannot read, showing that understanding is granted by God and involves human openness.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 29:7 teach about the fate of nations opposing God’s people?
options: Opposing nations will vanish like a fleeting dream
God is indifferent to foreign nations
Nations have autonomous power against God’s people
questions.correctAnswer: Opposing nations will vanish like a fleeting dream
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:7 states that the multitude of nations fighting against Ariel will be like a dream, emphasizing God’s judgment and the futility of opposition.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 29:20 specifically demonstrate?
options: Divine justice in punishing the wicked
Divine patience in waiting to judge
questions.correctAnswer: Divine justice in punishing the wicked
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:20 describes the terrible one and scorner being brought to nought and cut off, evidencing God’s justice.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does Isaiah 29:17 anticipate?
options: The restoration and flourishing of creation
questions.correctAnswer: The restoration and flourishing of creation
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:17 speaks of Lebanon being turned into a fruitful field and fruitful fields becoming forests, symbolizing restoration after judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 29:8 and 29:9 teach about spiritual blindness and human condition?
options: Spiritual blindness causes people to be like drunken men unaware of their condition
People freely choose to be spiritually enlightened
Physical blindness is the main issue
questions.correctAnswer: Spiritual blindness causes people to be like drunken men unaware of their condition
questions.explanation: Isaiah 29:8-9 describe nations as hungry or thirsty men dreaming they are fed or drunk but awakening empty, and people staggering as if drunk but not from wine, illustrating spiritual blindness.
